rows.gap: These conditional constructions express the bootstrap law with measurable variables, integrability and the usual almost-everywhere version interpretation.

comparisons.D19: Condition on the entire observed vector (X1,...,XT), using its generated sub-sigma-algebra. E-star of an integrable bootstrap quantity is condExp with respect to that sigma-algebra; Prob-star of an event is the conditional expectation of its indicator, or the event mass under a regular conditional bootstrap kernel. It is not conditioning on an equality event with positive probability assumed, and not merely conditioning on a fitted statistic. The conditional value is a random function of the observed data; the bootstrap randomness is integrated out. On the finite probability space setting the trimmed measure is finite, but measurability and integrability still need to be satisfied rather than using condExp’s zero fallback. Conditional kernels identify versions only almost everywhere under the data law, not at every imaginable sample vector.

Singular PSD covariance is allowed; positive definiteness is not required. multivariateGaussian maps a non-PSD input to a degenerate fallback, so checking PSD is essential to assert the prescribed covariance.
